Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1256 AM CDT Sat Jul 25 2026

Valid 251200Z - 261200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR PARTS OF
CENTRAL MT...AND ALSO ACROSS PARTS OF SD...

...SUMMARY...
Storms with scattered severe wind gusts are possible across parts of
Montana and South Dakota this afternoon and evening.

...MT into SD and vicinity...
An expansive upper ridge will remain anchored over much of the
southwest and central CONUS through the period. Very hot
temperatures are expected this afternoon from MT into the Dakotas.
Isolated to scattered storms within the hot and well-mixed
environment will result in a broad area of at least isolated
severe-wind potential. 5% wind probabilities have been expanded to
cover this potential, with 15% wind probabilities (equivalent to
categorical Level 2/Slight Risk) added across parts of MT and SD,
where terrain features may enhance storm coverage within the
favorable severe-wind environment. 

For parts of western/central MT, convection that develops by
early/mid afternoon near the high terrain is expected to spread
eastward into the hot and well-mixed environment. This convection
may be aided by a low-amplitude midlevel vorticity maximum moving
around the periphery of the upper ridge. Increasing storm coverage
and gradually strengthening mid/upper-level flow may allow for one
or more outflow-driven clusters to develop and spread
east-northeastward into early evening, with a threat of severe
gusts. Localized gusts of 75+ mph cannot be ruled out, especially if
deeper convection is able to spread into areas where very deep
mixing and heating to near/above 100 F occurs prior to storm
arrival. 

Farther east, very strong heating is expected across parts of
western/central SD, with temperatures in some areas potentially
rising to near/above 105 F. Low-level moisture will be relatively
sparse, but MLCAPE of near/above 1000 J/kg will be possible where
50s F dewpoints can be maintained within the well-mixed environment.
Initial storm development near the Black Hills will quickly become
outflow dominant as it spreads eastward, with an increasing threat
of severe gusts. Deep-layer shear will be somewhat favorable for
organized convection, and some guidance depicts development of a
persistent cluster or loosely organized MCS that moves eastward
across SD along a weak surface boundary. Should this occur, a
corridor of more organized severe-wind threat (with gusts
potentially near/above 75 mph) will be possible. 

...Northern/eastern MN into WI and Upper MI...
Conditional severe potential remains evident across parts of the
Upper Midwest, though confidence regarding storm coverage and timing
remains very low within the weakly forced environment. Moderate to
strong destabilization is possible along/south of a surface front
that is forecast to extend from northeast ND into northern MN/WI by
late afternoon. Effective shear of 50+ kt will be more than
sufficient for storm organization, but most guidance remains rather
muted regarding potential for diurnal storm development. If storms
are able to develop during the afternoon or evening, then a threat
for hail, damaging wind, and possibly a tornado could evolve. Even
if diurnal storm development is limited, vigorous elevated storms
may evolve within a warm-advection regime near/north of the front
late tonight, which would pose a threat for hail and perhaps locally
damaging wind. Confidence remains too low to include more than
Level-1/Marginal Risk equivalent probabilities at this time. 

...Northeast NV/northern UT into eastern ID...
Storm development is expected during the afternoon across parts of
northeast NV, along the western periphery of the upper ridge. These
storms will spread into adjacent parts of southeast ID and northwest
UT with time. Strong to locally severe gusts will be possible with
these storms as they move northeastward through a well-mixed
environment.  

...South-central/southeast AZ...
High-based convection is again expected across southeast AZ during
the afternoon, with initial downburst potential. Modest enhancement
to easterly flow along the southern periphery of the upper ridge may
allow for localized strong to severe gusts to spread westward into
parts of south-central AZ, before convection weakens later Saturday
night.

..Dean/Squitieri.. 07/25/2026

$$

Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1224 AM CDT Sat Jul 25 2026

Valid 261200Z - 271200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER THE UPPER
MISSISSIPPI VALLEY INTO UPPER MIDWEST...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms capable of mainly large hail and damaging winds
are possible from the upper Mississippi Valley and Great Lakes into
portions of the mid Missouri Valley on Sunday and Sunday night.

...Synopsis...

A dominant upper high will remain anchored over the central and
southern Plains with an associated ridge extending north into
central Canada. Within the periphery of the ridge, a belt of
enhanced mid-level flow will extend from the Pacific Northwest
through south-central Canada into the Great Lakes and middle OH
Valley. A series of weak mid-level disturbances will translate
through the stream of higher-momentum flow, the most notable of
which is a short-wave trough that will crest the ridge axis over
SK/MB. Modest height falls are expected downstream from that feature
from northern MN into the upper Great Lakes Sunday night/early
Monday.

At the surface, a cool front attending the SK/MB system will advance
through the northern High Plains into the ND-MN Red River Valley. A
weak front will settle south through northern parts of MN and WI
before stalling, while a separate frontal system extends from the
Southeast into the Midwest with another boundary.


...Upper Mississippi Valley and Great Lakes into the Mid Missouri
and Ohio Valleys...
Capping associated with the mid-level ridge and the subtle nature of
mechanisms to sustain forcing for ascent lead to considerable
uncertainty in the location, areal coverage, and intensity of
thunderstorms Sunday into Sunday night. That being said, a few
early-day thunderstorms appear possible across the upper Midwest
within a zone of warm advection and aided by the glancing influence
of a weak disturbance moving through the upper Great Lakes. The
storms would likely be elevated within a plume of moderate
instability and ample vertical shear, suggesting some potential for
large hail and damaging winds.

By afternoon, a reservoir of moderate to strong instability is
forecast across the Midwest with the various models indicating the
potential for diurnally enhanced thunderstorm development at various
locations from the mid MO Valley into lower MI. Confidence in any
one scenario remains low, and as such, a modest expansion of the
level 1/Marginal Risk was made across parts of the OH Valley to
account for the broad range of potential outcomes. Given the degree
of instability and seasonably strong vertical shear, higher severe
weather probabilities and related conditional intensity groups may
become necessary once forecast details become more clear. 

As alluded to in the synopsis, stronger forcing for ascent tied to
the approaching Canadian disturbance and surface front may support a
more focused area of thunderstorm development over MN Sunday night.
Subsequent upscale growth into a forward-propagating MCS appears
possible, which would increase the potential for a swath of severe
wind gusts.  


...Southeast...
One or multiple weak disturbances aloft are expected to overspread
the region, along with a slight increase in mid/upper-level winds.
In response, a weak surface low may develop across upstate SC, along
a subtle front/confluence zone in the area. Thunderstorms are
expected to increase in coverage and intensity through the afternoon
along the front and developing sea-breeze boundaries within a very
moist and moderately unstable air mass. Steep low-level lapses and
high precipitable water content will enhance downdraft potential
with an associated risk for locally damaging winds.

..Mead.. 07/25/2026

$$

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0228 PM CDT Fri Jul 24 2026

Valid 261200Z - 271200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER THE UPPER
MISSISSIPPI VALLEY INTO UPPER MIDWEST...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms capable of mainly large hail and damaging winds
are possible from the upper Mississippi Valley and Great Lakes into
portions of the mid Missouri Valley on Sunday and Sunday night.

...Synopsis...
Enhanced mid-level flow will round the central US ridge D3/Sunday,
overspreading portions of the Midwest and Great Lakes regions. Along
with the increasing flow, several shortwave disturbances will shift
across the region. At the surface, a low will develop across the
northern Plains/Upper Midwest with a surface front moving through
the northern Plains/Midwest by the evening.

...Upper Mississippi Valley into the Great Lakes...
Beneath strong upper-level ridging and a very moist air mass with
dew points in the 60s to mid 70s, an EML plume will advect eastward
across the High Plains into the Midwest/Great Lakes region. This
will result in a very volatile and strongly unstable but largely
capped air mass. While forcing for ascent will increase, lack of
discernible surface features and strength of the capping inversion
leads to low confidence in the exact evolution of thunderstorm
development. Hi-res guidance does suggest that a few isolated
supercells may develop. A conditional threat for large to very large
hail, damaging wind, and perhaps a tornado will exist with any
storms that can become rooted within the boundary layer, given the
presence of 35-50 kt deep-layer shear and the favorable unstable air
mass. 

As the front shifts south and east through the afternoon/evening and
forcing for ascent increases, storms may develop as far west as the
eastern Dakotas/Nebraska. It seems probable that a thunderstorm
complex could develop across some portion of the upper Mississippi
Valley, though confidence in the exact corridor remains low. This
will pose a conditional threat for a more focused corridor of
damaging wind potential.

..Thornton.. 07/24/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0337 AM CDT Fri Jul 24 2026

Valid 271200Z - 011200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Day 4/Monday...
A prominent upper high will remain centered over the central and
southern Plains with a belt of enhanced mid-level flow forecast
along the periphery of that feature from the northern Plains into
the Great Lakes. Within that flow regime, a short-wave trough is
forecast to translate through the Great Lakes in tandem with a
surface low and trailing cold front. A hot and moist boundary layer
is expected ahead of the front, yielding moderate to strong
instability by afternoon. Despite veered low-level winds,
strengthening mid/upper-level winds in the exit region of a jet
streak will contribute to sufficient vertical shear for organized
severe storms across portions of the Great Lakes into the OH Valley
Monday afternoon into night.


...Day 5/Tuesday...
The Day 4/Monday short-wave trough is forecast to evolve into an
upper low across southwest ON and the lower Great Lakes with an
associated belt of stronger cyclonic flow developing from the OH
Valley into the southern Mid-Atlantic and NC. At the surface, an
area of low pressure will develop from the lower Great Lakes into
central NY with a trailing cold front advancing through the upper OH
Valley, central Appalachians, and Mid-Atlantic.

Thunderstorms may be ongoing Tuesday morning along and ahead of the
front from the lower Great Lakes and upper OH Valley into the
Mid-Atlantic. Stronger heating is anticipated to the south of the
early-day storms from the southern Mid-Atlantic into NC, where
moderate to potentially strong instability is forecast. The
strongest instability will coincide with modestly strong deep-layer
shear to support some severe weather threat in those areas Tuesday
afternoon and evening.


...Days 6-8/Wednesday-Friday...
The 00Z ensemble means depict a slight westward regression of the
dominant mid/upper-level high with persistent troughing along the
East Coast. On the periphery of the high, a notable short-wave
trough is forecast to progress from the Canadian Rockies on
Wednesday through the Prairie Provinces on Thursday with modest
height falls along the international border. By Friday, there is
some model signal for another short-wave trough to move into the
upper MS Valley and Great Lakes regions. At the surface, a more
substantial cold front is projected to move into the northern Plains
on Thursday, and the upper Midwest and Great Lakes by Friday. 

A few severe storms appear possible in the Southeast and northern
Plains on Wednesday, the northern Plains on Thursday, and the upper
Midwest into the Great Lakes on Friday. Confidence in the magnitude
and areal extent of the threat is currently too low to delineate
additional areas.

..Mead.. 07/24/2026
